name: Asukayama
tagline: Tokyo in 29 minutes and Otemachi in 33 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000.
summary: The station is in Kita City, where the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 33 minutes to Otemachi, 34 minutes to Shinjuku, 38 minutes to Shibuya and 43 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. The station stands 16 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 18.7 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 16 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 4.7 m to 23.4 m, a difference of 18.7 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of less than 0.5 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 4 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is 0.5 to 3 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the small side for the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 16 clinics and 15 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 桑原病院, about 16 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 愛誠病院, about 25 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line).
congestion: The ministry's congestion survey does not publish figures for Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line). It covers the major commuter stretches, and this line is not among them.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥70,000 to ¥80,000 and 1K ¥100,000 to ¥110,000. 1LDK ¥150,000 to ¥160,000 and 2LDK ¥220,000 to ¥230,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

neighbours.lead: Oji is ahead on the number of lines and how close the centre is, but Asukayama is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection and quiet.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Asukayama. It reaches Otemachi 7 minutes sooner than Asukayama. One-room rents run about ¥9,000 higher.

neighbours.lead: Takinogawa-Itchome is ahead on quiet, but Asukayama is ahead on the number of medical facilities and how easy the shopping is.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Asukayama. It reaches Otemachi in about the same time as Asukayama.

leads.terrain: There are gentle slopes around the station, and which block you live on changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 11 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 6 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line) serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the high side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
